item.title: German Bundestag Lets Customs Freeze Crypto Over €100,000 Without a Criminal Case as the Bill Goes to the Bundesrat
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine German Bundestag Lets Customs Freeze Crypto Over €100,000 Without a Criminal Case as the Bill Goes to the Bundesrat The German Bundestag on Thursday approved a government bill that would let customs freeze cryptocurrency and other assets worth more than €100,000 when their lawful origin appears implausible, without first opening a criminal case. Permanent confiscation would still take a finance-court judgment. The measure still needs the Bundesrat’s consent before a planned Jan. 1, 2027 start, and the timing of that upper-house vote remains unclear. The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, a Finance Ministry overhaul to strengthen the customs administration and fight financial crime, on Nov. 12. The federal government introduced the bill on Sept. 30. The Finance Committee recommended passage on Nov. 11, with the Christian Democrats, Social Democrats and Alternative for Germany in favor, The Left opposed and the Greens abstaining. Crypto is covered but not singled out Crypto is covered expressly, using the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets definition, but it is not singled out. The same administrative procedure applies to cash, cars, real estate and other property. It reaches only “significant” assets: generally those worth more than €100,000, or more than €50,000 if the asset must be entered in a public register, such as vehicles or land. Because crypto is not registered that way, the €100,000 threshold applies. Customs may estimate the value, and closely related items can be treated as one asset. Customs offices — not Germany’s Financial Intelligence Unit, which the same bill strengthens separately — may freeze those assets for up to 30 days without a criminal case if there are factual indications the origin is not lawful, meaning lawful acquisition “does not appear plausible.” A finance court may extend that hold once by 150 days. That extension is decided by a single judge, without a hearing, in an order that cannot be appealed. Filing a confiscation application stops the clock until the court rules, so the often-cited 180-day period is not a hard cap. Permanent confiscation still requires a finance-court panel to be convinced the origin is unlawful. The committee shifted that decision away from a single judge. Owners must be told they are not required to produce records, and anything they do provide may be used in tax and criminal cases. The official justification says mere silence, or a denial of knowledge, will as a rule not be enough to prevent confiscation. Supporters and critics split Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said in August that if suspects cannot show assets were legally acquired, “the Porsche or the Rolex are gone for now.” In Thursday’s debate, Social Democrat Ingo Vogel told the Bundestag that criminally acquired assets do not enjoy constitutional property protection, and that the bill is “no automatic confiscation” and “no blanket reversal of the burden of proof.” The Bundesrat, in an e

item.title: Harvard Holds 3.04 Million Bitcoin ETF Shares Steady
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Harvard Holds 3.04 Million Bitcoin ETF Shares Steady Harvard Management Company left its stake in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust unchanged at 3,044,612 shares in the third quarter, a position valued at $144.1 million as of Sept. 30 and now worth about $110.6 million after bitcoin’s slide. The university’s endowment manager disclosed the holding in a Form 13F filed Friday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. The share count is the same one Harvard reported on June 30 and on March 31. At 10:40 a.m. ET Monday, IBIT traded at $36.32, putting the stake at about $110.6 million, a paper decline of roughly $33.6 million, or 23%, from the value in the filing. The Sept. 30 close of $47.34 matches the price implied by the reported value. The same 3,044,612 shares were worth $101.4 million on June 30 and $117.0 million on March 31, so the position rose in value during the third quarter as bitcoin recovered, then gave back a large share of that gain after the quarter ended. Even after the November slide, the stake is still worth more than it was at midyear. IBIT was Harvard’s eighth-largest position among 18 holdings in a 13F portfolio valued at $3.95 billion, or about 3.6% of that publicly disclosed book of U.S. securities, which does not include the rest of the endowment. The largest holding was Space Exploration Technologies, reported at $1.29 billion. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was second, at $616.5 million. That ranking is a sharp change from late 2025, when the bitcoin ETF was Harvard’s largest publicly disclosed position. First bought in 2025, then cut, then held Harvard first reported an IBIT position in its filing for the quarter ended June 30, 2025: 1,906,000 shares worth $116.7 million. It had not listed the fund in earlier 13Fs, including the report for March 31, 2025. By Sept. 30, 2025, Harvard had tripled the stake to 6,813,612 shares, valued at $442.9 million, making IBIT its largest public holding. The endowment trimmed that position by about 21% in the fourth quarter of 2025, to 5,353,612 shares worth $265.8 million, and opened a first stake in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust of 3,870,900 shares, valued at $86.8 million. It cut the bitcoin ETF again in the first quarter of 2026, by about 2.31 million shares, or 43%, to the 3,044,612 shares it still reported on Sept. 30, and sold the Ethereum fund entirely. The latest filing lists no other bitcoin or crypto ETFs. The remaining IBIT position is still larger, in share terms, than the 1.91 million shares Harvard first disclosed. Gold now outweighs the bitcoin ETF Harvard’s gold ETFs are now much larger than its bitcoin position. The same 13F lists 1,161,000 shares of SPDR Gold Shares worth $442.2 million, the portfolio’s third-largest holding, and 1,980,085 shares of the iShares Gold Trust worth $154.6 million. item.title: Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday denied Custodia Bank’s petition to review the Federal Reserve’s refusal to give the Wyoming bitcoin bank a master account, ending chief executive Caitlin Long’s years-long fight for direct access to the central bank’s payment rails. The case, Custodia Bank, Inc. v. Federal Reserve Board of Governors, No. 26-62, is listed under “certiorari denied” on the Court’s Monday order list . The denial leaves in place a Tenth Circuit ruling that regional Federal Reserve Banks have discretion to reject even eligible applicants, and it closes the last court path Custodia had to force the Fed’s hand. A master account is a bank’s account at a Federal Reserve Bank, and the entry point to Fedwire and other payment services. Without one, a state-chartered bank has to rely on a correspondent institution to move money. Eligible, then turned away Custodia is a Wyoming special purpose depository institution, a charter that bars it from making loans and requires dollar deposits to be fully reserved in liquid assets. After receiving that charter, it applied for a master account at the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City in October 2020. In January 2021, the Kansas City Fed confirmed the bank was legally eligible and told it there were “no showstoppers.” In August 2021, Custodia also applied for Federal Reserve membership. While those requests sat pending, the Board of Governors in August 2022 published guidelines for evaluating master-account applications. The rules put firms that are neither federally insured nor supervised by a federal banking agency into “Tier 3,” the group that “generally receive[s] the strictest level of review.” Custodia fell into that bucket. On January 27, 2023, the Kansas City Fed denied the master account, citing an “unprecedented” business model “narrowly focused on crypto-asset activities” and concluding the risks were “highly likely” to be “inconsistent with safe and sound banking practices.” The same day, the Board denied Custodia’s membership application, saying approval “would be inconsistent with the financial, managerial, and corporate powers factors.” The last Custodia appeal fails Custodia had already sued the Fed and the Kansas City Fed in June 2022 over the delay. On March 29, 2024, U.S. District Judge Scott W. Skavdahl in Wyoming ruled that the Federal Reserve Act gives Reserve Banks discretion to grant or deny master accounts, dismissed Custodia’s Administrative Procedure Act claim for lack of a final agency action, and granted the Kansas City Fed summary judgment. The Tenth Circuit affirmed on October 31, 2025, in a 2-1 decision Bitcoin Magazine covered at the time. item.title: Hong Kong to License Crypto Dealers and Custodians by Year-End
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Hong Kong to License Crypto Dealers and Custodians by Year-End Hong Kong will introduce a bill before the end of the year to bring crypto dealers, advisers, asset managers and custodians under a licensing regime, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Monday, even as the city has approved only two of 36 first-round applicants to issue stablecoins. Chan delivered the remarks in a keynote at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum in Hong Kong. “Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter, extending licensing to those who deal in, advise on, manage and act as custodians of digital assets,” he said. The plan would amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, expanding a regime that now covers virtual asset trading platforms, the government told the Legislative Council on Nov. 4. A tight gate for stablecoins “On stablecoins, we have moved forward step by step. Of the 36 applicants in the first round, two received licences in April, and both have since launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoins,” Chan said. He said the emphasis is on “genuine use cases and credible business models,” citing cross-border payments as an example. The Stablecoins Ordinance took effect in August 2025. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority granted the two issuer licenses this April, the government said in that earlier Legislative Council reply. Chan did not name the two issuers or say when a further application round might open. The low approval rate is the point. Hong Kong is trying to build a regulated digital-asset market without opening the door to every issuer that applies. Same activity, same regulation “Our principle is simple: same activity, same risks, same regulation,” Chan said. On tokenisation, he said funds offered to the public in Hong Kong have grown about seven-fold in a year, and that since last month two tokenised money market funds have traded around the clock on a licensed platform. “Our approach is consistent: the same requirements as for conventional products, with additional safeguards for the new risks.” Those figures line up with a fuller count the government gave on Nov. 4. As of the end of September, the Securities and Futures Commission had authorized 17 retail tokenised products, including 13 tokenised money market funds, with about HK$10.3 billion in assets in their tokenised classes. Two of those money market funds began round-the-clock secondary trading on licensed platforms on Oct. 26. “Above all, we are firm on one point: Decentralisation does not mean less accountability,” Chan said. Completing the perimeter Hong Kong already licenses virtual asset trading platforms. The new bill is meant to pull dealing, advisory, management and custody work into the same ordinance, a step the government has framed as streamlining the legal perimeter rather than writing a new one from scratch. item.title: Sweden’s H100 Taps Coinbase Prime and Deribit for Its 3,506 Bitcoin Treasury as It Courts Family Offices
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Sweden’s H100 Taps Coinbase Prime and Deribit for Its 3,506 Bitcoin Treasury as It Courts Family Offices Swedish bitcoin treasury company H100 Group said Monday it will use Coinbase Prime and the Deribit derivatives exchange for custody, trading and financing of its roughly 3,506 BTC, a move it says supports both its bitcoin-per-share goal and a push to serve wealthy investors. H100, which trades on Stockholm’s NGM Nordic SME under the ticker H100, announced the partnership in a release Monday morning. The company and its subsidiaries will use Coinbase and Deribit, which Coinbase owns, for custody, trading and financing, it said. H100 valued its holdings at about SEK 2.3 billion, or $226 million, based on a bitcoin price of $64,600 on Nov. 15. It also has about SEK 219 million ($22 million) in outstanding convertible loans that carry 0% interest, mature on July 9, 2030, and equal less than 10% of the stated value of its bitcoin. The release did not disclose fees, collateral terms or borrowing limits. It also didn’t say whether H100 has drawn on any financing, how much of its bitcoin will sit with Coinbase, or whether it is moving coins from another custodian. Prime brokerage for a bitcoin balance sheet H100 described Coinbase’s offering as the crypto version of a bank’s prime brokerage desk, bringing custody, financing and trade execution under one roof. The trading itself will be run in-house. PDI AS, a wholly owned trading and technology unit, builds the software and trading systems used to manage H100’s bitcoin, and the company said those tools operate “with protecting H100’s Bitcoin holdings as the first priority.” “This partnership gives H100 stronger tools for our own balance sheet, and we use them on our own Bitcoin first,” Executive Chairman Sander Andersen said. “Bitcoin per share remains the measure we run the Company by, and these tools are there to help us deliver on it, not to add risk.” Andersen added that this is “the first of several” partnerships, “and the next is already under way.” He did not name the next partner. Lauren Abendschein, head of institutional sales at Coinbase, said bitcoin treasury companies “have grown into an established part of our institutional client base,” and that their priorities are custody, “liquidity when the market moves, and financing against the same balance sheet.” From health tech to family-office ambitions The second goal is bigger. H100 said it wants to become what majority shareholder Geir Harald Hansen, in a June 11 letter to shareholders, called “a leading European alternative and digital asset manager.” It will start with family offices and high-net-worth individuals looking for a partner on bitcoin investments and financing, and said it will share details as products launch. H100 began as a health-tech company before adopting a bitcoin treasury strategy in 2025. It agreed in January to buy Swiss treasury firm Future Holdings and closed that deal in February. item.title: Strive (ASST) Buys 251 Bitcoin for $17.5 Million as Shares Drop 10% Premarket
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys 251 Bitcoin for $17.5 Million as Shares Drop 10% Premarket Strive bought another 251 bitcoin last week for $17.5 million at an average of $69,853 per coin, Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole posted Monday, lifting total holdings to 43,404 BTC. “Strive acquired 251 $BTC for $17.5M at an average cost of $69,853 per bitcoin, bringing total holdings to ₿43,404,” Cole wrote. A Monday 8-K filing shows the purchases ran from Nov. 7 through Nov. 13, inclusive of fees and expenses, and took the Dallas company’s stack up from 43,153 bitcoin a week earlier. Cole said Strive raised $10 million through its SATS at-the-market program. The filing puts that total at $10.02 million in gross proceeds from the sale of 104,478 shares of the company’s 15% Series A perpetual preferred stock. Strive sold no Class A common shares and no shares of its variable-rate SATA preferred during the week. Cash and cash equivalents fell $22.3 million to $465.3 million as of Nov. 13. Cole also posted a preferred dividend coverage figure of 133 months and an amplification ratio of 76%, two metrics the 8-K does not break out. The 251-coin add is larger than the 29 bitcoin Strive bought the prior week at an average of $75,721 and the 124 bitcoin it bought in late October at $80,526, but it remains a fraction of the October sprint that built the stack. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 before Strive acquired 15,124 coins between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a 6,182-coin buy . The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds and later lined up a $1 billion SATS at-the-market program, the facilities that have funded the larger purchases. Effective common shares outstanding were unchanged at 127,331,109. SATS shares outstanding rose to 7,141,037, while SATA remained at 14,030,176. Strive still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred, marked at a fair value of $50.5 million as of Nov. 13. On Nov. 12, the board raised the regular dividend rate on SATA to 13.25% for periods beginning Dec. 1 and declared daily December cash dividends of $0.0502 a share on SATA and $0.0569 a share on SATS, which continues to carry a 15% rate. Those daily payments total $1.1044 a share on SATA and $1.2518 a share on SATS for the full month. Strive shares drop in premarket trading Strive’s Class A shares fell around 10% in Monday premarket trading to $19.34 as of 8:45 a.m. ET, from Friday’s close of $21.36. The move tracks a broader selloff in bitcoin-linked stocks. Strategy, the largest public corporate holder, was down 8.1% in premarket trading to $102.60 as of 8:45 a.m. ET, from Friday’s close of $111.62. ASST has already given back a large share of its October run. The stock closed Oct. 21 at $30.75 and Oct. 30 at $22.19. item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 After Weekend Plunge to $62,000
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 After Weekend Plunge to $62,000 Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Monday morning, down about 2% from Sunday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The world’s largest cryptocurrency is trying to hold its ground after a weekend plunge to $62,000, as tech stocks slid ahead of Nvidia’s earnings and traders braced for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. The selling that broke Friday’s low on Saturday morning did not stop there. Bitcoin slipped under $64,000 Saturday afternoon and dropped below $62,000 in the 8 p.m. ET hour on some exchanges, its lowest level since July 14. It bounced back above $64,800 within the hour and reached about $66,100 early Sunday before sellers returned. The bitcoin price has spent most of the past day between $64,000 and $65,000. The slide has been punishing for leveraged traders. About $2 billion of crypto positions were liquidated over a 24-hour period during the weekend, the vast majority of them long bets. Bitcoin is now down 17% in November and has posted six straight weekly losses. Tech stocks and rate fears weigh on the bitcoin price Stock futures offered little help on Monday. Contracts on the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.5% and S&P 500 futures slipped 0.7%, while Nvidia fell 3% in premarket trading. Investors weighed a Financial Times report that former CEO Jensen Huang and his allies are discussing a campaign to reinstate him, a week after his resignation sent bitcoin below $72,000 . Nvidia reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, and options markets imply an earnings-day move of about 7% in either direction, Pepperstone’s Chris Weston told Reuters. Bitcoin has traded in step with chip stocks for much of the past week, so a weak report could add to the pressure. Rates remain the other weight on the bitcoin price. Traders fully price a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s December meeting, with odds of a half-point move near 8%, CME FedWatch data show. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.12% on Monday after jumping 29 basis points last week, and higher yields have lifted the dollar to its strongest level since April 2025. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in San Francisco later Monday, and minutes from the last Fed meeting are due Wednesday. Strategy slides as ETF outflows stretch to seven sessions Bitcoin-linked stocks fell with the coin. Strategy (MSTR) was down 8% in premarket trading and Strive (ASST) fell 9%. Strategy is also facing index-fund selling after MSCI removed it from its USA index , forcing index funds to sell by Nov. 30. Spot bitcoin ETFs shed another $185 million on Friday, their seventh straight day of outflows, bringing losses since Nov. 5 to about $1.91 billion. That run follows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) bleeding $2 billion over nine straight sessions. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 Million as It Spends $228 Million Buying Back Preferred Stock
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Adds 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 Million as It Spends $228 Million Buying Back Preferred Stock Strategy bought another 485 bitcoin last week. A Monday 8-K filing shows the Saylor-led firm spent $33.4 million at an average of $68,887 per coin between November 9 and November 15, lifting total holdings to 850,849 BTC bought for $64.20 billion at an average of $75,452. The coins were funded with net proceeds from MSTR common stock sales. Strategy sold 2,087,040 shares for $244.7 million, put $33.4 million into bitcoin, used $206.3 million of those proceeds to buy back its STRC preferred and parked $5.0 million in USD Cash. No preferred stock was sold under the ATM during the week. The STRC buyback was larger than that ATM slice. Strategy retired 2,282,510 STRC shares for $228.1 million, funding the other $21.8 million with interest earned on its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. It still has $332.2 million left under its preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its MSTR buyback authorization, with about $18.1 billion of MSTR still available under the ATM. The $228.1 million preferred repurchase was nearly seven times the $33.4 million bitcoin spend. The 485-coin add was also less than half the 1,036 bitcoin Strategy bought the week before. BREAKING: Public companies Strategy and Strive bought over $47 million worth of Bitcoin during this dip Strategy: 485 BTC Strive: 251 BTC pic.twitter.com/alNNfxbQY2 — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 16, 2026 A deeper hole under the treasury The filing lands as the spot bitcoin price sits well below Strategy’s average cost. At the time of writing it trades near $64,100, about 15% under the $75,452 basis, leaving the stack roughly $9.7 billion underwater on paper. A week earlier, the same treasury was only modestly below cost after bitcoin slipped under $75,000. The new coins do not close that gap. They were bought at $68,887, above today’s price but well below last week’s $79,012 average, and they shaved the company’s overall cost basis by only $4, to $75,452 from $75,456. Strategy now holds more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. The pace of buying has slowed as the firm has put more ATM cash into preferred buybacks than into bitcoin, a pattern that also marked the prior week’s purchase. Between June 30 and August 10, Strategy sold bitcoin in four consecutive filings to fund preferred dividends and STRC buybacks before flipping back to accumulation. Dividends stay at 12% as the reserve is drawn Strategy used $18.9 million of its USD Reserve during the week to pay preferred dividends. As of November 15, the reserve stood at $4.75 billion and USD Cash at $151.2 million. On November 15, the company said it will keep the regular dividend rate on STRC at 12.00% for record dates in December. Daily STRC dividends for the month total $1.00 per share. item.description: ▶ Bitcoin Magazine Peruvian Bull: The Yen Carry Trade and Bitcoin’s Road to $300k Roberto Rios, the Peruvian Bull and author of the Dollar End Game Substack, joins Spencer Nickels to explain how the yen carry trade connects to Bitcoin’s road to $300,000. He traces the trade from the Plaza Accord to today’s estimated $3 trillion to $6 trillion. He explains why the Bank of Japan’s aggressive rate hikes are starting to crack it, and how Japan’s yen interventions push up U.S. Treasury yields. In the short term, he warns that a carry trade unwind like August 2024 can “break Bitcoin lower.” Long term, he argues that high rates force the government to borrow more and the Fed to eventually print more, which he calls “massively bullish for Bitcoin.” He also says “this cycle we’re going to go to $300,000.” Host: Spencer Nichols — Bitcoin Magazine Peruvian Bull— Founder, Lima Research LLC & Author, The Dollar Endgame Check out Peruvian Bull’s Youtube Channel here: https://www.youtube.com/@UCEcuGzyEYOcNG32SBAGM7Sw Partnership Enquiries: Let’s find your fit!
